title: Session 07 — Ironhold and the Forge Council
sourceFile: Session 07 - Ironhold and the Forge Council.md
html:
Session 07 — Ironhold and the Forge Council

[!important] 🎙 START RECORDING before the session opens. Check the mic level, confirm the file is writing, and only then read the opener aloud. If you forget until later, note the timestamp when recording began so the recap workflow can pad the earlier beats from memory.

Session 7 opens mid-scene at Halvor’s back warehouse door. The party frees Mira and the children, confronts Halvor, and learns about Lis. Late that night, Vrass finally speaks to Torren. The next day the town wakes up to the news that the Forge Council will vote in four days — and the Veil, the Dominion and Ironhold’s politics all reach for the party at once. Session 8 is the vote.

Session opener (read aloud)

It’s a little before ten o’clock on the night of 25 Frostfall. Ironhold’s streets have gone quiet; the foundry glow paints the low clouds orange. You’re standing in a narrow, unlit alley at the back of a merchant’s compound on the edge of the Council Ward. In front of you is a timber-and-stone warehouse, and its back door is held shut by a heavy chain and an old padlock. Sera Vey is at your shoulder, barely breathing. Somewhere on the other side of that wall are her sister Mira and Mira’s two children, taken from Stillbrook by a man called Halvor. Beside Sylas, a small spectral shape hangs in the dark — the Fey he called out of himself on the walk here — waiting.

Where you are and what you’re doing. You came south as caravan guards and arrived as the Wayward Company: paid, lodged at the Grey Kettle, and owed a dragon. Torren’s life belongs to Vrass. Sylas still carries a sealed Coin Cipher chest that everyone else believes the dragon took. Mother Hessa knows Torren is Guilded Veil, and told him he wasn’t the only Veil name she’d heard that night. And tonight, rather than wait for morning, you came for Mira.

The chain is cold. The lock is old. What do you do?

Table decisions locked for Session 7

  • Opens mid-scene at Halvor’s back warehouse door, ~21:50, 25 Frostfall.
  • Sylas’s Summon Fey is active (concentration, 1 hour). Cast on approach at ~21:35 — about 45 minutes remain when play starts. Track it.
  • Sera is present. The zombies are in the wagon at the Kettle stables.
  • Vrass’s whisper lands late that night, after the raid — read aloud at the table.
  • Kellan’s cell reaches Torren via Mother Hessa — a note under his breakfast plate the next morning.
  • The Forge Council vote is in four days — extraordinary session on 30 Frostfall. Announced in-world on the morning of 26 Frostfall. The vote is Session 8’s climax.
  • 25 Frostfall (raid night) is a Stillday; 26 Frostfall is a Daystar. Corporal Vasso drinks at the Broken Anvil on Daystar and Hearthen nights — so he is there on the 26th, and again on vote night (30 Frostfall, a Hearthen).

The clocks the party is now running against

Clock Deadline Source
Lis Halvor 7 days from tonight — Davos Hark sells her on 2 Sablemourn. Aeloria is 3 days hard ride. Halvor, Beat 2
Forge Council vote 30 Frostfall — 4 days from tomorrow morning. Public notice, Beat 4
Vrass’s Heart of Ironhold Before the dark moon — roughly 3 weeks. Vrass, Beat 3

The squeeze is deliberate. If the party stays for the vote (30 Frostfall) and rides hard for Aeloria the next morning, they arrive with about a day to spare for Lis. It’s possible — barely. Let them work that out.

Beat 1 — The breach (~21:50, 25 Frostfall)

The space

The alley. Narrow, unlit, cobbled, a gutter running down the middle. Timber back-walls on both sides, the occasional shuttered window. It smells of wet stone and the stables two doors down. Watch patrols pass the alley mouth at midnight and again at three. Until midnight, it’s quiet.

The back warehouse. Timber-and-stone, single storey. Two rooms inside: - Front office — Halvor’s trading office. A desk, a ledger cabinet, crates of low-value cloth and nails, a cold fireplace. Cor Brackin’s straw pallet is against the wall by the door. An ale jug on the floor. A small dying fire. - Back holding room — 12 by 15 feet. One small barred window high on the back wall. Two straw pallets, a bucket, a water jug, one shared blanket. Timber door, iron bolt on the office side.

The yard (between warehouse and house). Cobbled, ~30 feet across. One well on the eastern wall. Alley gate padlocked from the yard side.

The front house. Two-storey timber townhouse. Lamplight in one ground-floor window — Halvor’s office. He’s awake.

Who’s where at 21:50

  • Cor Brackin — front office of the warehouse. Three ales in. Awake but sluggish, sitting on his pallet with the jug.
  • Mira, Wil (11), Elsie (7) — back holding room. Mira is awake. Wil is asleep against the door.
  • Halvor — front house office. Drinking alone in the dark.
  • Nella (housekeeper, 51) — asleep upstairs in the front house.
  • Tobin (stable boy, 14) — asleep upstairs in the front house.

Ways in

  • The back door (chain + padlock). Pick the padlock: DC 10 Thieves’ Tools. Quietly snap the chain: Strength DC 15 (loud on a fail — Brackin hears).
  • Knock. Brackin answers through the door: “Warehouse is closed. Halvor’s business. Come back tomorrow.”
  • Alley window (shuttered). Prying the shutter: DC 12. Small — a halfling or the Fey fits; others don’t.
  • Over the yard wall. Athletics DC 12. Lands them in the yard, between the house and warehouse — Halvor’s window has a view of the yard (Halvor’s passive Perception 11).
  • The Fey. It can scout through the high barred window and report what it sees: three people on pallets, a woman awake, a man in the next room with a jug.

Cor Brackin

Human, 34, broken nose, unwashed blond hair, leather jerkin over a stained shirt. Short sword he doesn’t like to draw. He folds.

  • Persuasion or Intimidation DC 12 — “This isn’t worth dying for.” He surrenders and asks to leave.
  • 5 gp — he’s on the Aeloria road by dawn and never says a word.
  • 10 gp — he’ll also tell them everything he knows and testify against Halvor if asked.
  • Combat — MM Thug (AC 11, HP 32, mace +4, two attacks). Morale breaks below half HP; he runs.
  • What he knows: Halvor’s daughter is the reason. “Some counting-house bastard in Aeloria has her.” He was hired through an Aeloria middleman called Kettleman. The key to the holding-room bolt? There isn’t one — it’s just a bolt. He’s never bothered learning the prisoners’ names.

“You’d let me leave? Right. Fine. Right. Give me my coin and I’ll be on the Aeloria road by dawn. Not a word from me to anyone. I mean that.”

Freeing Mira

The bolt slides back in one motion. Inside: the children first — two pale faces looking up from the pallets — and Mira standing behind them, hands on their shoulders, absolutely still. Wil is on his feet between them and the door with his fists up.

“Who’s there? — If you’re Brackin, I’m warning you, the boy’s awake.”

  • Sera is here. The reunion is immediate and wordless. Give it one beat — Mira says “You’re alive. He knocked you down and I didn’t know—” — then her eyes go to the children and she’s back in charge.
  • “Wil. Wil, stand down. They’re friends of your aunt.”
  • Mira has been listening for a week. If anyone asks what she knows:
  • Brackin drinks from eleventh hour and is usually asleep by midnight.
  • Halvor hasn’t come into the room since the first night. “He paces. Out there. I heard him cry once.”
  • He says a name at night — “Lis.” And “twelve days.” Over and over. “I think she’s the reason we’re here.”
  • They’ve been fed properly. Halvor buys the food himself. “That’s what I can’t understand.”

This is not a combat encounter. The tension is emotional. Brackin folds; Halvor breaks.

Beat 2 — Halvor (~22:15)

The space

Halvor’s office, ground floor of the front house. One lamp on the desk, turned low. Papers scattered — ledgers, letters, a list of numbers that keep getting crossed out. One wine glass on the floor, tipped over. The room smells of stale wine. The door to the parlour is ajar. A small framed charcoal sketch of a girl of about fifteen sits face-down on the desk.

Halvor

Human, late fifties, merchant gone to seed. Good coat, unbuttoned. Grey stubble. Hasn’t slept properly in two months. He knows exactly what he’s done.

  • If the party comes in loud (crossing the yard, a fight at the warehouse): Halvor is standing in the office doorway with a candle and no weapon. “Is it Brackin? What’s — who are you?”
  • If the party comes in quiet: he’s at the desk, head in his hands. He doesn’t hear them until they speak.
  • Nella wakes if there’s noise. She comes down in her nightgown, sees the party, sees Mira and the children in the yard, and goes very still. She has decided, for a week, not to ask. She will not defend Halvor. She will cry.
  • Tobin (14) will hide upstairs unless called. Knows nothing about the back room.

The break

  • First, he lies. “They owe me money. It’s a lawful debt. You’ve no right.”
  • Insight or Persuasion DC 15 — or automatic if the party says the name Lis (Mira gave it to them): “You’re not the man holding this family. Someone is holding you.”
  • He breaks:

“My daughter. Davos Hark in Aeloria has my Lis. He took her as collateral when I couldn’t pay. Seven days. Seven days until he sells her into one of the houses on the docks. I needed thirty gold. The Marcus family had thirty gold once. They could have it again. I didn’t — I fed them. I never touched them. Take them. Take them all. Just — help me with Lis. Please.”

  • What he can tell them about Davos Hark (only if asked):
  • Counting-house in Aeloria’s Merchants Rise district.
  • Lis is held in a back-room apartment above it. Two thugs guard her.
  • Davos isn’t the worst of it — he’s being squeezed too. “Someone above him wants the money moving north. I don’t know who.” (The chain points toward Aurum-pressured merchants in Aeloria. Do not name Aurek this session.)
  • Halvor owes Davos far more than 30 gp — the 30 was a down payment to buy time.

Resolution paths

  • Pay the Marcus debt themselves (30 gp). Family freed, debt cleared. Halvor flees Ironhold in shame within the week. Lis is still in danger.
  • Force release, walk away. Family freed. Halvor publicly ruined within a week (Nella talks). Lis is lost off-screen.
  • The full solution — promise to help with Lis. Halvor releases the family freely and swears off the Marcus debt. The party commits to Aeloria. Becomes the return-hook arc. Best outcome.
  • Hand him to the Watch. Kidnapping is a crime. Halvor goes quietly. Lis is lost. Stillbrook is satisfied; the party is not.

Sera’s reaction when Halvor says “Lis”: anger first, then something quieter. She sits down beside Mira and doesn’t say much for the rest of the scene.

Mira’s view, if asked: “I don’t know. He fed us. He also took us. I don’t know what that makes him. I just want to go home.”

Where the family goes

They can’t stay here. Mother Hessa takes them in at the Kettle without a question if the party brings them — Sera, Mira and the children share a room for the price of a single (Hessa waives it if Orin asks). They’ll want to go home to Stillbrook as soon as they can travel.

Beat 3 — The walk back, and Vrass (~23:30)

The space

The Merchants’ Quarter after the eleventh bell. Lamps burning low in iron brackets. A few late drinkers. The Kettle’s sign — the grey enamelled kettle — creaking on its bracket. Foundry Row’s glow on the clouds to the south. Somewhere a dog barking. Cold.

The whisper

When Torren has a still moment — at the back of the group on the walk, alone in his room, at the Kettle’s yard pump — the whisper lands. Read it aloud at the table. Frame it clearly: only Torren hears this.

“Little sworn-halfling. Listen carefully… I have an assignment for you.”

“There is a stone in this town. A jewel that glitters like fire. They call it the Heart of Ironhold. Steal it and bring it to me before the dark moon. Do not fail me in this small thing.”

The dark moon is about three weeks away. See The Heart of Ironhold for what the Heart is, where it’s kept, and what happens to Ironhold if it’s taken.

If Torren tries to answer: Vrass hears him. He’s patient, amused, and not interested in negotiation tonight. “You will find a way. You found a way on the road.” Then nothing.

If Torren asks what the Heart is: Vrass doesn’t explain. “Something they love. That is enough.”

What the party may find out over the next day (don’t volunteer — let them ask): every Ironholder touches the Heart on their coming-of-age day; it’s kept beneath the Forge Council Hall’s dome; Priestess Elisara holds the only key. Stealing it would hurt the town physically — forges failing, fires, the Anvilhome’s hearth going cold.

End of the first half. Good place for a break.

Beat 4 — Morning at the Kettle (26 Frostfall, Daystar)

The space

The Grey Kettle at breakfast. Long taproom, low sun through the front windows, fresh bread out at seven. Smells of yeast and rosemary and hot pewter. Half the tables taken by merchants eating fast. Hessa moving between the kitchen and the taproom.

Patrons this morning — pick two: - A pair of Merchants’ Quarter clerks in matching black coats, reading the same broadsheet over each other’s shoulders and arguing about it in whispers. - A heavyset dwarf in a Stonecut green coat, eating alone, very slowly, reading a small book. (Not a named NPC — but if the party is curious, he’s a Precision Guild journeyman and his master is Gundri Stonebreath.) - Two Watch soldiers coming off night shift, eating eggs, too tired to talk. - A young woman with ink on her fingers — a scribe — copying something from a ledger and not eating.

The note

Under Torren’s breakfast plate — Hessa sets it down herself — is a folded square of paper. On the outside, a small chalk sign Torren recognises: the Veil’s mark for “safe meeting.” Inside:

Tallow Row, Rustpocket. The chandler with the blue door. Noon bell. Come alone or come with the ones you trust. — K

Hessa won’t explain. If asked: “A boy left it before the bread was out. I didn’t see his face. Eat your eggs.”

The vote is called

Mid-breakfast, the Council crier comes down the main street ringing a handbell and reading a notice, which is then pasted to the Kettle’s front post:

By order of the Forge Council of Ironhold: an extraordinary session of the Council will sit on the thirtieth day of Frostfall, at the noon bell, in the Council Hall, to vote upon the motion of Master Corvan Drake of the Ingots Guild concerning the Aurum Dominion’s proposed contract for arms. The session is open to citizens and visitors. — Bryndis Ashveil, Chair.

The taproom goes quiet, then loud. Overheard reactions (pick two): - “Four days. Drake wants it done before anyone thinks too hard.” - “Ashveil had to call it. She’s chair. Doesn’t mean she likes it.” - “Double market rate. My cousin’s shop would be rich in a year.” - “And owned by Aurum in ten.”

Hessa, quietly, to whoever’s closest: “If you’ve any business with the Council, you’ve four days to do it.”

The family

Sera, Mira and the children come down for breakfast. The children eat like they haven’t in a week. Mira wants to get home. If the party isn’t heading north, Brenna’s next run to Stillbrook leaves in five days — Hessa can arrange it.

Beat 5 — The Merchants’ Quarter, and Envoy Veris (mid-morning)

The space

Ironhold’s main market street in full swing. Stalls under canvas awnings, guild halls with their banners out, moneylenders’ doors with brass plates. Carts of ingots rumbling toward the southern gate. Smell of hot iron, horse, and roasting chestnuts. The Council notice is pasted on every second post. People are standing in knots reading it.

Street flavour — pick two: - A Blades Guild apprentice pasting a hand-written counter-notice over the Council one: “ASK WHAT IT COSTS.” A Watch soldier tears it down; the apprentice runs. - A chestnut seller shouting prices and Council opinions in the same breath. - Two Ingots Guild journeymen in Drake’s red armbands handing out cups of free cider “courtesy of Master Drake.” - A Celestium dwarf caravan heading south, the drivers ignoring all of it.

Envoy Veris Caelthorn

He crosses the party’s path — coming out of the Halloran Cloth Emporium with a parcel, or stepping down from a carriage outside Renwick’s counting-house. Two Aurum Sentinels in gold-trimmed half-plate flank him; four Ironhold Watch soldiers trail behind as diplomatic escort.

Human, 32, tall, slim and immaculate, a crystal-laced silver pin at the throat marking him as Aurum nobility. Smiles often — never warmly. Polite. Condescending. Coolly curious.

  • He notices Sylas immediately. Light purple skin — a rare tiefling colouring, and Veris (a Kaelthorn cousin, a wizard, and a collector of bloodlines) knows what it means.

“Forgive me. Aurora Peaks blood — and not just any blood. The old curse-line. Fascinating. May I ask your house?”

  • Sylas can decline. Veris doesn’t press. He notes it either way.
  • If the party engages on the vote: Veris is gracious and gives nothing. “Ironhold will decide what Ironhold decides. The Dominion offers partnership. That is all.”
  • If anyone mentions the Watch corporal rumour: a flicker. “Envoys speak to many people. It’s rather the point of us.”
  • He leaves with a small bow and a card with his name, “should the house of the curse-line wish to correspond.”

Consequence: Veris files Sylas. Within a fortnight, Princess Selene’s Crystal Shards hear of him. (Vaeloran already knows everything about Sylas — this is the Dominion learning, not Vaeloran.)

Common folk see “unusually pale purple, but he’s a tiefling — they come in odd colours.”

Beat 6 — Tallow Row: Kellan Bracewell (noon bell)

The space

Tallow Row is a crooked Rustpocket lane of chandlers, soap-boilers and rag merchants. It smells of hot fat and lye. Timber tenements lean over the street. Washing strung between windows. Children everywhere.

The chandler with the blue door — a narrow candle shop, rows of tallow dips hanging from the ceiling like bones. A heavy woman behind the counter (Gessa, the landlady — Veil-friendly, says nothing) nods at Torren’s mark and points at the curtain behind her. Behind the curtain: a trapdoor. Below it: a cellar, and beyond the cellar wall, a roughly cut opening into the Old Mines — Ironhold’s founding-era tunnels. Cold air. Lamplight.

Kellan is waiting in the first chamber of the old tunnel, sitting on an upturned crate with a lamp at her feet. Two of her operators stand in the dark further back — not threatening, just there.

Kellan Bracewell

Human, 38, short (5‘2”), mousey brown hair in a plain braid, grey-green eyes — a face people forget within the hour. Dressed like a Merchants’ Quarter clerk. Very still. Ironhold’s Guilded Veil Veilmaster. She’s been in hiding for nineteen days.

What she wants from Torren — and she gets straight to it:

“Six documents. I have two. The Watch has one and doesn’t know it’s thin. Mara Volk has three. If we can put five together in front of the right people, this ends. I have twenty operators and no way to move openly. You can move. I hope you see where this is going.”

What she’ll tell them: - Drake framed her with forged Naturus-cult papers because her cell undercut his contracts. He doesn’t know she’s Veil — he thinks she’s a smuggler working for a rival smith. - She has two of the six forgeries — she gives them copies now if the party agrees to help. - Mara Volk (Merchants’ Quarter fixer) has three. She’ll sell — at about 50 gp each, or a package deal if the party is clever. - The Watch has one — logged by Corporal Vasso, the officer Drake used. “He drinks at the Broken Anvil. Daystar and Hearthen nights. It’s Daystar.” - Vasso can put Drake’s hand on the papers. Documents plus a witness = the framing collapses in public. - Where it lands: the Council floor on 30 Frostfall. If the framing collapses in front of the Council, Master Ren Vestic — who hates being played — won’t vote with Drake. - She knows the vote count: 5 for, 3 against, 1 undecided (Councillor Merla Vinn). “Vinn reads contracts. Give her something real to read.”

What she offers: if the framing collapses and the contract fails, the Ironhold Veil owes the Wayward Company — twenty operatives, the Old Mines, and discreet help when they need it.

On the Coin Cipher: Kellan knows Warehouse #14 is Cipher, shares the Old Mines with them by convention, and stays out of their business. If the party mentions a chest, she goes still: “Don’t tell me anything about the Cipher you don’t want them to know I know.”

On Torren: she knows of him — Merric’s network, Stonegate before that. “Wenzel’s halfling. I heard you were sworn to something on the road. I’m not going to ask.”

On her brother Denny: if anyone mentions him, the stillness cracks for a second. “He thinks I count coins for a living. Keep it that way.”

Beat 7 — Afternoon options (choose what the party wants)

The party has a few hours before evening. Let them choose. Each option is self-contained.

A. Mara Volk — the documents

Mara’s tea-room, upstairs over a stationer’s shop in the Merchants’ Quarter. Small, warm, very tidy. A brass kettle. Two chairs. Shelves of ledgers with blank spines. Mara herself: half-elf, 63 but looks forty, short silver-gilt hair, grey eyes that rarely blink, clothes you forget you saw.

  • She serves tea, asks what they need, names a price.
  • The three Drake documents: 50 gp each, 150 gp total, or 100 gp plus a favour if the party negotiates well (Persuasion DC 15). Half up front. Delivered within the hour — she has them in the building.
  • She sells any political read at 25 gp: “Osgood is Drake’s for the price of two suppers. Vinn can’t be bought — she can only be convinced. Vestic hates being taken for granted.”

B. The Cinders — Sylas and Rustpocket

If Sylas goes looking for Oman’s family on Slag Lane (first turning east off the Broken Anvil): three adjoining tenement flats, washing on the line, kids on the stairs. Elder Vessa Cinder (82, white hair, one milky eye) sits Sylas down and feeds him stew before she’ll let him say anything. Warm, sharp, watchful.

  • Maren Cinder (37) runs the Broken Anvil’s kitchen and knows Vasso’s schedule, his complaints, and that he’s been “drinking Aurum gold.”
  • Rax Cinder (34) works Drake’s Furnace and saw the workshop fire Drake covered up — he’ll corroborate Bram’s account if the party ever needs it.
  • Kess Cinder (21) works at the Anvilhome and reads everything. A small, warm beat for Sylas if he wants it.
  • See Cinder Family.

C. The Forge Council Hall — looking around

Open to citizens by day. The great gold-domed hall in the Council Ward. Polished stone floor, nine high-backed seats in a crescent, an observer gallery. The reliquary corridor leads off the main hall to a heavy oak door — locked. A night porter, Rennie (62, not alert), sleeps in an alcove by the front door after dark.

  • Torren casing the Heart: he can learn the layout, the porter, the oak door (lock DC 12) and that the niche inside has a dwarven lock (DC 18) — Elisara holds the only key, on a thong around her neck. He can’t get in during the day without being noticed.

D. Bryndis Ashveil — the Grand Foundry

The Grand Foundry, Foundry Row: the biggest forge in Ironhold, roaring at full shift, sparks and noise and sweat. Bryndis — dwarf, 172, iron-grey braids, scarred forearms — receives the party in a small office above the forge floor that shakes every time a hammer falls.

  • She’s cautious with strangers. If they mention Kellan or the vote, she listens.
  • She suspects Kellan was framed and can’t prove it.
  • If the party shows her any of the documents: “Bring them to the chamber. Not to me. If I wave them about, it’s politics. If you put them on the floor, it’s truth.”

E. Brother Daven Soltan (optional — Orin)

The small Temple of Luminos in the Merchants’ Quarter. Brother Daven knew Merric years ago. An emotional beat for Orin if there’s time. See Brother Daven Soltan.

Beat 8 — Five o’clock: Orin and Hessa

Orin’s dinner date. Hessa has the snug at the Grey Kettle set for two — a candle, a carafe of the Merchants’ Quarter red, a mutton pie she made herself. She’s changed her apron for a clean one. That’s as dressed-up as she gets.

What Hessa gives Orin over dinner (she likes him; she’s not selling): - “Merla Vinn sat in that corner last week with the whole Aurum contract and a pencil. Read every page. Nobody else on that Council has.” - “Osgood eats at Drake’s table. Has done three times this month.” - “Veris has had supper in this snug twice with two men I don’t know. I didn’t like either of them.” - If Orin mentions the Heart: Hessa sets down her fork. “Nobody would. Nobody would ever.”

Keep it warm. This is a small pleasure in a heavy session.

Beat 9 — Daystar night at the Broken Anvil (optional, if the party goes)

The space

The Broken Anvil, Rustpocket. Two storeys of soot-stained timber sagging east, a sign with a broken anvil half worn away. One long taproom — bar down the left, mismatched tables for eighty, a rough hearth always burning at the back. Kitchen is a serving hatch (Maren Cinder behind it). Loud, smoky, smells of ale, sweat and hot lard. Foundry crews off shift. A flat fiddle somewhere. Riven (owner) behind the bar, watching everything.

Patrons tonight — pick two: - A Drake’s Furnace crew — six men and two women, soot to the elbow, loud about a shift bonus that never came. - Bram — half-orc, 22, six and a half feet of lean, ashen-skinned apprentice in a scorched leather apron; corner table, back to the wall, one ale. - Four labourers arm-wrestling for coppers and losing to the dwarves among them. - Denny Bracewell — big, young, forge-burned forearms, drinking alone and watching the door.

Corporal Vasso

Front table, close to the door. Big, loud, Watch greens on even off-shift, nose broken twice. Drinking too fast.

  • Buy him a drink — he talks.
  • Sympathise about the promotion (Persuasion DC 12) — he vents for twenty minutes: twelve years of nights, passed over for Sergeant Hollis.
  • Show him Drake used him (Persuasion DC 15, or automatic with the documents in hand) — confusion → humiliation → fury. “He bought me drinks for a month. He said I should be a sergeant…”
  • Once turned: he’ll fetch the Watch’s copy of document six from the evidence chest (night shift, one night’s notice), and testify at the Council that Drake handed him the papers in person.
  • The Aurum purse: he took 5 gp from Veris’s aide for a “conversation about Watch security.” The aide asked who holds the keys to the reliquary chamber. He’s ashamed. If he testifies, he should confess the purse first or Drake will use it to discredit him.

Denny vs Vasso (optional complication)

If Denny works out who Vasso is — “Which one of you is Vasso? Which one?” — he goes for him. Bar fight. Riven ends it in three rounds. The party can step in, and in doing so meet both men at once. See Denny Bracewell.

End of session — choose one

  • The ledger. Back at the Kettle, Sylas (or whoever) finally opens Halvor’s papers, or Kellan’s documents, and sees Drake’s hand on everything. Four days.
  • The card. Veris’s card sitting on Sylas’s pillow at the Kettle. Nobody put it there that the staff will admit to.
  • The hearth. Torren, alone, looking up at the gold dome of the Council Hall in the dark, Vrass’s words in his head.

Session 8: gather the evidence, work the councillors, and the vote on 30 Frostfall.

Forge Council quick reference (for planning; the vote is Session 8)

5 votes to pass. Baseline: 5 for, 3 against, 1 undecided.

Seat Vote Lever
Corvan Drake (Ingots) For None
Ren Vestic (Armours) For Public Kellan-framing reveal → abstains
Rell Tavish (Mail) For Follows Vestic’s lead
Brannic Wold (Fittings) For Bram’s foundry-safety testimony → abstains
Councillor Osgood (Civic) For (soft) Evidence of Drake’s gifts → abstains
Bryndis Ashveil (Blades, Chair) Against —
Gundri Stonebreath (Precision) Against Can publicly endorse Vinn
Vaelin Rook (Ornaments) Against —
Councillor Merla Vinn (Civic) Undecided Evidence, a real terms analysis, or Gundri’s backing

Full detail: Forge Council of Ironhold.

NPC roster for Session 7

  • Mira · Wil · Elsie — the family. Freed in Beat 1.
  • Sera Vey — present for the raid.
  • Cor Brackin — folds.
  • Halvor — breaks. Lis, Davos Hark, seven days.
  • Nella (housekeeper) · Tobin (stable boy) — Halvor’s household. See Halvor’s Compound.
  • Vrass — the whisper.
  • Mother Hessa — the note, the family’s room, Orin’s dinner.
  • Envoy Veris Caelthorn — the Sylas encounter.
  • Kellan Bracewell — Tallow Row, the Old Mines.
  • Mara Volk — three documents.
  • Corporal Vasso · Denny Bracewell · Bram · Riven — the Broken Anvil.
  • Bryndis Ashveil — the Grand Foundry.
  • Cinder Family · Oman — Rustpocket.
  • Brother Daven Soltan — optional.

Pacing notes
